messages.subject: [statnet_help] Computational time required by netlogit
messages.body_plain:
Dear statnet users,

I am trying to estimate a QAP model with a binary network as a dependent variable using the command netlogit with the double semi-partialling method. I have 435 nodes and 9 independent variables. I have estimated the same model using UCINET routine for the same permutation method and the valued network as dependent variable. The computation time in UCINET was around 1 hour with 2000 permutations but the netlogit estimation is taking more than 5 hours with 1000 permutations. 
Is this normal? Would you advice me to use a different permutation method with netlogit?

Thanks
Paola

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Computational time required by netlogit
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Paola -

Criscuolo, Paola wrote:
> Dear statnet users,
> 
> I am trying to estimate a QAP model with a binary network as a dependent 
> variable using the command netlogit with the double semi-partialling 
> method. I have 435 nodes and 9 independent variables. I have estimated 
> the same model using UCINET routine for the same permutation method and 
> the valued network as dependent variable. The computation time in UCINET 
> was around 1 hour with 2000 permutations but the netlogit estimation is 
> taking more than 5 hours with 1000 permutations.
> Is this normal? Would you advice me to use a different permutation 
> method with netlogit?
> 

That kind of procedure is always going to be slow on a 10x435x435 array, 
and the netlogit routine is not built for speed.  In terms of alternate 
permutation methods, there's not much theory at this point (of which I 
am aware) on the properties of these test procedures in the logistic 
regression case; so, caveat emptor.  I would probably opt for a network 
permutation model (see the netperm package) under these circumstances, 
myself, but it depends on what you want to infer....

-Carter

messages.subject: [statnet_help] statnet installation
messages.body_plain:
Dear Caroline,

They was a problem with the MacOS X PPC build. Try reinstalling now using:

library(updatestatnet)
update.statnet.now()

which will force a reinstall.

The Mac OS X (tiger) version was built on a Mac Pro (Intel Core Duo) with a
cross-compiler for the PPC version. Please let me know if you have problems
loading it. It would be good to ensure the build works on older G4 and G5
Mac.

Best,

Mark

I succesfully installed statnet with the newest build of R but was unable to get
the ergm function to work.  I tried a very simple (and abritrary) example but it
would basically never finish running and would sometimes close R down.  So, I
did something like:

r<-network(rgraph(10))
ergmtest<-ergm(r~edges)

but could not get this to finish computing.  Any ideas as to what is going on? 
I did this on a Windows based computer if that is helpful.  Also, I had no
problems running statnet on earlier versions of R on different comuters.


Thank you,

Jeff Smith
